Commentary.Commentary: Right then! It's been an exciting month or so of Under 19 cricketing action and the favorites, India have gone on to win their fifth title. With this our coverage of the Under 19 World Cup 2022 has also ended. Hope you all enjoyed it. There's a lot of cricketing action going around the globe though. The senior Indian side will take on West Indies in the first ODI on Sunday, the 6th of February. That match begins at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT). Do join us for that match. Till then, take care and goodbye!
Yash Dhull now lifts the trophy and the Indian team is jubilant in celebration as they pose for the winning photograph!

Under 19 World Cup-winning captain, Yash Dhull says that it's a proud moment that they have managed to achieve something for the national side. He adds that they spent a lot of time together and bonded like a family which helped them to improve as a team. He mentions that England made a good comeback with the bat and they just needed to keep a cool head. States that the coaching staff was brilliant and they have learned a lot from them.
The Indian players now come up one by one to collect their winner's medals from Sir Curtley Ambrose. A proud moment for each and every one of these young men.

England Under-19 skipper, Tom Prest says that opting to a bat first, they got a nervy start and they would have liked to bat better. Mentions that James Rew deserved a century but missed out. Tells that they have got a good bowling unit and they believed that they could defend 189. Says India batted well though. Says that he has made friends from other teams as well. Adds that their parents and families have flown in to support them. Tells that the boys played really well.
The English players now come one by one to collect their runners-up medals. What an outstanding tournament they have had!

South Africa's Dewald Brewis is adjudged the PLAYER OF THE TOURNAMENT! He broke the long-standing record of most runs in a single tournament with 506 runs and even picked up 7 wickets throughout the course of the tournament. Baby AB must have made Ab de Villiers proud with that achievement.

Raj Angad Bawa is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his 5/31 with the ball and a vital contribution of 35 runs with the bat as well. Bawa says that it always feels great to contribute in any match but when it's the finals it's even more special. He mentions that he just tried to execute the plans laid out by the coaches and on being asked if he prefers to ball or bat, Bawa says that he prefers a bit of both.
... The Presentation Ceremony ...

Ravi Kumar now comes down for a quick chat. He says that the feeling is great and is speechless. Tells that the coaches just told them to do their best. Mentions that they just said it might or might not be your day but one should give their 100%. Informs that there was something on offer in the first innings and he made the most out of it. Says that his first wicket was his favorite.

Shaik Rasheed, the Indian vice-captain is down for a chat. He says that winning the World Cup feels great. Mentions that he is really happy. States that it was about assessing the scoreboard and taking it accordingly. Ends by saying that he just wanted to play his normal game.

VVS Laxman is up for a chat now. He congratulates the selection committee. Mentions that it was a challenge for them to get this side and they have done a splendid job. Tells that the boys have worked really hard. Says that there hasn't been much domestic cricket in India and they haven't played consistent cricket for a long time. Adds that they won the Asia Cup recently and the preparations for the World Cup were fantastic. Tells that it's about developing them further on into successful cricketers.

Hrishikesh Kanitkar, the Indian Head coach is up for a chat. He says that it was a great performance and is happy with the result. Mentions that they have learned a lot from this. Tells that they were looking to bat as well but they thought that there is something in the wicket as well and they exploited the conditions. On being asked about Nishant Sindhu, he says that he has got a good head on his shoulders and thinks about the situation very well. Ends by saying that it is a great platform to showcase your talent at a very young age.
Time to get a few reactions to the Indian title win...

There's always pressure in the final but India never ever looked to be under any sort of pressure given their body language. After a disastrous start, a couple of 40 plus stands and a well-compiled half-century from Shaik Rasheed put India well ahead of the game. Rasheed gave away his wicket and soon, the skipper, Yash Dhull too fell. It was the partnership between Nishant Sindhu and Raj Angad Bawa worth 67 runs that steadied the ship yet again. India kept on losing wickets at crucial times and were finding it difficult to find the fence. Sindhu though showed excellent composure and saw the team through as he hit a brilliant half-century. Dinesh Bana then came in and hit a couple of sixes to seal the title win. India really were dominant throughout the tournament and deserve the win today as well.

At the interval, almost no one would have given England a chance to win the match or even take it as deep as they managed to do. Boyden gave them the best start possible by picking up Angkrish Raghuvanshi for a duck in the very first over. After that though, England focused on keeping the rate down rather than picking up wickets and allowed the opposition to get the required runs below 100. The fight was not over though. The English bowlers gave it their all and Tom Prest kept on chopping and changing the bowling as well. James Sales and Tom Aspinwall bowled with great heart and the spinners were tight. Sales picked up a couple of wickets as well but in the end, he just couldn't hold his nerves.

What a fabulous contest we have witnessed here in the final! A run chase which looked simple to begin with but England somehow made a match out of it and have pushed India all the way. In the end, India have managed to keep their calm and win a record-extending 5th Under 19 World Cup title. Nishant Sindhu has been the hero for India and Dinesh Bana definitely added the finishing touches.

SIX! Dinesh Bana take a bow! He finishes things off in style. A juicy full toss, on middle and leg. Dinesh Bana hammers it over long on. Enough power on that one to clear the ropes. Dinesh Bana is pumped up. The Indian players start running onto the pitch to celebrate. They are all around the park. INDIA UNDER-19 WIN THE MATCH BY 4 WICKETS!
SIX! Dinesh Bana you beauty! Pressure? What pressure? Fuller in length, on the pads. Dinesh Bana simply flicks it over deep square leg for a maximum. He is all smiles. Scores level now.

FIFTY! What a knock from Nishant Sindhu! He is guiding his team over the line. First fifty for him and he couldn't have asked it to come at a better time. Short of a length, on middle. Nishant Sindhu works it to deep mid-wicket for a single. He raises his bat and soaks all the applause.

FOUR! Beautifully picked up by Nishant! A poor, poor ball from James Sales at this stage. Length ball, going down the leg side. Too easy for a man who is batting on 45. Nishant Sindhu just helps it on it's way to fine leg for a boundary. Moves to 49 now!
James Sales (7-0-34-2) is brought back into the attack.
Back of a length, outside off. Sindhu punches it to sweeper cover for a single. 12 needed from 18 balls. India are two hits away from clinching their fifth title.
Good-length ball, angling in on middle. Dinesh Bana swipes it to across to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Very full, Bana drives it back to the bowler.
Good-length ball, on off. Dinesh Bana mistimes his chop aand under-edges it back to the keeper.
Dinesh Bana is in at number 8.

OUT! TAKEN! Tom Aspinwall bags his second wicket and maybe, just maybe there's still glimmer of hope for England. Fuller, outside off. Kaushal Tambe reaches out for that one and tries to drive. But the ball goes straight to backward point where Rehan Ahmed takes a good catch moving to his right. England players are pumped up. Can England pull off a mircale?
Commentary.Howout: c Rehan Ahmed b Tom Aspinwall

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on middle. Kaushal Tambe defends it off the back foot.
Tom Aspinwall (8-0-40-1) is back on.
A googly, on middle. Kaushal Tambe safely tucks it on the leg side for a single. Rehan Ahmed finishes his spell here and he remains wicketless in his 10-over quota. 14 needed now from 24 balls.
Floats it up, on off. Tambe goes back and defends it out.
Slower through the air, outside off. Driven towards covers.
Comes 'round the wicket and bowls a loopy ball, on middle. Blocked out.
Tossed up, on middle. Kaushal Tambe blocks it out.
Googly, short and outside off. Nishant Sindhu slaps it to long off for one.
Smart from Sindhu! Full and straight, pushed down to mid on for one. 16 needed off the last 5 overs.

FOUR! Nishant Sindhu desperately needed a boundary and has got it now. Dragged down, around middle and leg. Sindhu hangs back and pulls it in front of sqaure. The fielder from deep mid-wicket runs around and puts in the despairing dive but it goes in vain.
Four dots in a row now! Fullish ball, on off. This is pushed back to the bowler.
The dots keep on building and so does the pressure. Brilliant bowling from Boyden. Around off, Sindhu can't get it away on the off side.
Shorter in length, Sindhu mistimes the pull down to mid on. 21 needed off 34 balls.
A length ball, on off. Sindhu defends it out on the off side.

A googly, around leg. Kaushal Tambe doesn't pick it up at all and looks to work it away leg side. He misses and gets rapped on the pads. A huge appeal from the English players but its been turned down. Missing leg probably.
Around off. Tambe watchfully blocks it out.
Around leg, this is worked through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! That'll ease the nerves a bit. Tossed up, outside off. Nishant Sindhu leans in and creams the cover drive through the inner ring on the off side and picks up a boundary.
Quicker one, around leg. Sindhu pushes it back to the bowler.
On middle. Blocked out.
Kaushal Tambe is the new batsman in.

OUT! TAKEN! Is there a late twist in the tale? Bringing back Boyden into the attack has proved to be rewarding. Just short of a length, on off. Raj Angad Bawa hangs deep in his crease and looks to pull. It's a lazy shot from Bawa in the end as his feet don't move and he mistimes the pull shot straight towards mid on. The skipper, Tom Prest takes the simplest of catches and Bawa is sent packing. 26 still needed off 42 balls. Can England pull off a miracle here?
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Prest b Joshua Boyden

Commentary.Commentary: Angled into middle. Sindhu punches it through extra cover and rotates the strike.
A good-length delivery, around off. This is eased through the cover region for a single.
Back of a length, outside off. Bawa looks to cut but checks his shot and taps it back onto the deck.
A length ball, on middle. Sindhu punches it down to long on for one more.
Fullish delivery, angled into middle. Bawa presents the full face of the bat and pushes it down the ground for a run.
This is dragged down, around off. Bawa backs away and slaps it through cover-point for a single. 30 required now off 48 balls.
Around off. Bawa can't get it through the cover region.

NOT OUT! A bit of drama out there in the middle. This is short and a bit wide. Raj Angad Bawa makes room to cut but edges it down to first slip. The ball though seems to have come off the keeper's left boot and straight into the palms of the slip fielder. The third umpire checks it from quite a few angles and we can see that the ball might have just brushed the left boot off the keeper but definitely bounced off the turf as well.

An appeal has been sent upstairs for a catch. The soft signal is NOT OUT. Replay shows that the ball bounced off the surface and went into the hands of the first slip fielder. The ball was too close to Alex Horton's boot and maybe that's why that created a doubt in his mind. The decision stands not out.

Edged and four! Another googly, beautifully bowled, around off. Raj Angad Bawa is drawn forward to drive but gets an outside edge and there's no slip there to take the catch. The ball just races away into the fence.
On off, Bawa defends it off the front foot.
A googly, on off. Bawa gets right behind the line of the ball to block.
Full and straight. This is pushed towards mid on for a quick single.
Uppish but safe! Short and wide, Bawa throws his hands at it and slices it over backward point for a couple.
Nails the yorker yet again does Tom Aspinwall. Around middle and leg, Bawa jams it out on the leg side.
Well bowled! A full and pacey delivery, close to the off pole. Bawa is well beaten as he looks to drive.
Yorker length delivery, on off. Bawa manages to jam it out.

SIX! Stand and deliver! These two are in a hurry now. A length ball, on middle. Raj Angad Bawa just stands tall and clubs it high and long, well over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie. The 50 partnership is up as well between these two.
Powerplay 3 signalled by the umpire! The fielding side can now have up to 5 fielders outside the 30-yard circle until the end of the innings.

SIX! Terrific blow! First maximum of India's innings and it comes off Nishant Sindhu's bat. In the slot, outside off. Nishant Sindhu gets down on one knee and slog-sweeps it all the way over long on for a biggie. A mighty blow from the southpaw. 44 needed from 60 balls.
Outside off, pushed to backward point.
Flighted ball, on middle. Sindhu keeps it out.
Googly, outside off. Raj Angad Bawa hangs back and cuts it towards deep cover for a single.
Shortish, around off. Bawa flicks it to mid-wicket.
Loopy ball, on middle. Tucked to mid-wicket for a run.
The last roll of the dice from England here. Rehan Ahmed (6-2-12-0) comes back into the attack.
An lbw appeal but turned down again! Fuller, on leg. Raj Angad Bawa misses his flick and gets hit on the boot. Tom Aspinwall appeals but the umpire shakes his head. The ball was pitching outside leg.
Nails the yorker, on off. Raj Angad Bawa jams it out.
Good-length ball, on middle. Raj Angad Bawa gets behind the line and blocks it out.
On a length, on leg. Nishant Sindhu tucks it to deep square leg for a run.
WIDE! Short and outside off. Nishant Sindhu leaves it alone. Wide called for height.
Short of a length again, on middle. Pulled to deep square leg for one.
Short of a length, outside off. Defended by Bawa.
Very full, outside off. Nishant Sindhu slices his drive to backward point.
Fuller, outside off. Raj Angad Bawa drives it through covers for a single.
Full and outside off. Nishant Sindhu drives it towards sweeper cover for a single.
Flighted, full and on off. Nishant Sindhu keeps it out.
On middle and leg. Sindhu pushes it on the leg side.

Huge appeal from the England players but not given! Tossed up nicely, on leg. Nishant Sindhu looks to flick but misses. He gets hit on the pads. Tom Prest pleads the umpire for an lbw but he says no. Good decision from the umpire as it was going down leg.

DRINKS! India have lost 4 wickets but with just 57 runs more required, all they need is one decent partnership. James Sales has given England an outside chance by getting rid of both Rasheed and Dhull. Now England have to believe and try their hardest. Sindhu and Bawa have looked really good so far and if they remain composed, then India should get over the line here.
On a good length, on off. Raj Angad Bawa gets behind the line and solidly knocks it back to the bowler. Nice partnership building along between these two.
Fuller, on off. Sindhu drives it to sweeper cover. Only for a single.
On a length, on leg. Nishant Sindhu clips it to deep square leg. He hares back for the second run and gets it easily.
Short of a length, on off. Sindhu rocks back and defends it out.
On leg, nudged to mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length, on off. Bawa cuts it towards backward point. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but hits the back of Nishant Sindhu instead.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Full and ngling down the leg side, Nishant Sindhu gets down on one knee and sweeps it behind square on the leg side. Couple of bounces and into the fence.
Tossed up, on off. Sindhu presses forward and keeps it out.
Loopy ball, outside off. Pushed through cover-point for a run.
On middle, turned to mid-wicket for a single.
Full again, outside off. Nishant Sindhu drives it straight towards covers.
Full and on middle. Nishant Sindhu prods and pushes it to mid on.
Length this time, around leg. Bawa taps it onto the leg side. 67 runs needed now off 90 deliveries.
Full, around leg. Bawa flicks it straight to mid-wicket.
A length ball, around middle and leg. Blocked out.
A length ball, angling down leg. Bawa tucks it away behind square on the leg side and comes back for the second with ease. Boyden just hurt himself a bit as he slid to cut off the ball.
FOUR! Full and straight, driven straight back past the bowler and for a boundary. Lovely shot from Raj Angad Bawa.
Full, around off. Bawa leans in and drives it straight to mid off.

Quicker one, close to the off pole. Nishant Sindhu backs away to cut but gets a thick outside edge which runs away fine. Joshua Boyden chases it down from short third man and saves two crucial runs for his team.
On a length, around middle and leg. Bawa works it off the back foot towards deep mid-wicket for just a single.
Drifted into middle and leg. Sindhu presses forward and works it through mid on for a run.
Quicker one, darted into off. Sindhu manages to block it out.
On middle, pushed towards mid on for a single.
Bawa looks to drop and run but Sindhu isn't interested. Flatter one, on off. Bawa nudges it towards cover-point.
A length ball, on the pads. Bawa turns it on the leg side for a run. 78 runs needed off 102 deliveries.
Full, on middle. Bawa can't get it past silly mid on.
Fuller delivery, sliding into leg stump. Bawa looks to work it leg side but gets a huge inside edge onto the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire isn't interested.
Around the top of off. Bawa stays solid in defense.
Short and wide, this is slashed down to the third man region for a single.
Short of a length, angling across the off stump. Bawa stands tall and thumps it through cover for a run.
Bawa uses his feet to push the ball, towards mid on and sets off for a quick single. It is a tight run but they do make it through.
Drifted into middle and leg. Bawa keeps it out.
On middle. Bawa defends it off the front foot.
Quicker and flatter, on off. Bawa punches it off the back foot towards extra cover.
Sliding into middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket.
This is dragged down, outside off. Sindhu rocks back and cuts it towards cover-point. The fielder over there makes a half-stop down to his left and the batters get a single.
Back of a length, around off. Sindhu strokes it through the cover region for a run.
Banged in short, around off. Sindhu looks to uppercut it but misses.
A length ball, skidding on from around leg. Bawa gets it off the inner half of the bat towards square leg for a run.
Length again, closer to the off pole. Sindhu edges it down to third man for a single.
FOUR! Width on offer and Nishant Sindhu duly obliges! A length ball, wide outside off. Sindhu cuts it behind point and the ball races away into the fence.
Back of a length, around middle. Sindhu hops back to defend.
Fraction short, on off. Bawa defends it towards covers. Another tidy over comes to an end. 90 needed from 120 balls.
Floats it up, on middle. Tucked on the leg side for a quick run. 100 up for India!
Full again, on middle. Sindhu defends it watchfully.
Loopy ball, outside off. Nishant Sindhu cuts it to point.
Full and on leg. Bawa works it on the leg side for a single.
Flatter ball, on middle. Raj Angad Bawa presses forward to block.
Tom Prest (5-0-12-0) brings himself back into the attack.
Overpitched, on off. Nishant Sindhu pats it back to the bowler. A superb over from Sales. A wicket and just a single off it.
Fuller, outside off. Bawa drives it through extra cover. Gets off the mark with a single.
Good-length ball, on middle. Bawa gets behind the line and meets it with a dead bat.
On a length, on middle. Bawa defends it off the front foot.
Raj Angad Bawa who earlier got a five-fer walks out to bat.

OUT! TAKEN! What a game James Sales is having! An important contribution with the bat and now comes back for his second spell and knocks over the two set batters. This is a tad bit short, around middle and leg. Yash Dhull picks it up and whips it towards the backward square leg fence. The ball goes flat and hard and George Bell runs around from deep square leg to take a good running catch. Just like the vice-captain, the skipper too has a rush of blood and England have made the most of it.
Commentary.Howout: c George Bell b James Sales

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length ball, outside off. Yash Dhull defends it towards covers.
Drifting it on leg, turning in. Nishant Sindhu works it off the pads to deep square leg for a couple of runs.
A googly, on off. Sindhu punches it to point.
Quicker ball, outside off. Nishant Sindhu leaves it alone.
Loopy ball, outside off. Nishant Sindhu defends it out.
On the pads, Nishant Sindhu looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. A stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire.
On off, defended towards covers.
Nishant Sindhu is in at number 5.

OUT! TAKEN! Fifty and out for Shaik Rasheed! He throws his wicket away. Good-length ball, outside off. Shaik Rasheed swipes it across the line. Does not time it well and ends up slicing it over mid-wicket. James Rew settles under it. The ball pops out of his hands but he takes it on the second attempt. A good knock comes to an end. India Under-19 lose their third wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c James Rew b James Sales

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.
A low full toss, outside off. Yash Dhull drives it through covers for a brace.

FIFTY! Shaik Rasheed is carrying on with his form! Two consecutive half-centuries for him. Back of a length, outside off. Shaik Rasheed taps it towards backward point. This is a superb knock from India's vice captain but the job is not done yet and he would look to convert this into a bigger score.
Full and on off, pushed towards covers.

A full toss, outside off. Shaik Rasheed plays it towards covers for a single. The fielder does well to dive to his left and stop the ball. But he throws it at the striker's end. A needless throw and the batters run one more.
James Sales (3-0-17-0) is back into the attack.
A maiden from Ahmed! A googly, on middle. Dhull picks it and flicks it to mid-wicket for no run. Second maiden over for Rehan Ahmed!
Short and outside off, Yash Dhull mistimes his chop towards covers.
On middle, Dhull rocks back and works it to mid-wicket.
Floats it up outside off, Yash Dhull drives it with an angled blade but straight towards cover.
Full and on middle, blocked out.
Tossed up, outside off. Pushed towards covers off the front foot.

Angled into middle and leg, Yash Dhull works it through mid-wicket for a single. Rasheed wants the second but Dhull sends him back. At the halfway mark, India are 89/2! 101 more runs are needed off the remaining 25 overs.
Around off, Rasheed cuts it to deep point for one more.
On the pads. This is worked towards mid-wicket for a run.
Drifted down leg, Dhull pushes it to the right of the bowler and looks for a single. Bethell though dives down and makes a good stop.
Quicker one, around off. Rasheed pushes it out towards extra cover for a single.
Short and wide, Shaik Rasheed is all over it and cuts it behind square on the off side for a couple.
Flatter one, around middle. Dhull works it onto the leg side.
This is dragged down on middle. Yash Dhull rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Slower through the air, on the pads. Dhull defends it out.
On a length, around off. Dhull hangs back and punches it towards silly mid on.
On off, pushed onto the off side for a single.
FOUR! Glorious cover drive from Shaik Rasheed! Tossed up, outside off. Rasheed just makes room and goes inside-out through covers and picks up another boundary.
It's looking comfortable at the moment for India. A touch short and wide, Rasheed punches it off the back foot through cover for a run.
Flatter one, around off. Dhull just guides it to sweeper cover for one more.
On off, this is driven through the cover region for a single.
WIDE! Quicker one, down the leg side. Rasheed looks to paddle it fine but misses. Wided.
A rare misfiled and it costs two crucial runs. Short and wide, there to be punished. Shaik Rasheed cuts it straight to Rehan Ahmed at point but Ahmed spills it and the batters come back for two.
This flighted, full and on off. Rasheed gets to the pitch of the ball and strokes it towards cover.
Darted into middle. Rasheed strides out to defend.
Around middle, Rasheed pushes it towards wide mid on for a run. 11 coming off that over, a good one for India.
FOUR! Terrific piece of timing from Shaik Rasheed. Short again and there's width on offer. Rasheed goes onto the back foot and cuts it hard and behind point for a boundary.
Short and wide, Dhull throws his hands at it and hits it towards deep point for a single.
FOUR! Short but not short enough. Yash Dhull slaps it to the left of mid on and the ball races away into the fence.

Direct hit would have been interesting. Back of a length, on middle. Shaik Rasheed pushes it towards mid on and sets off for the single right away. The shy at the bowler's end is missed and that would have been really tight.
Aspinwall hits the length hard and bowls it outside off. Rasheed taps it onto the off side.
Flighted ball, full and on off. This is pushed back to the bowler.
Quicker one, wide of off. Dhull guides it down to backward point.
Shorter in length, around off. Dhull goes on the back foot to work it through cover for a couple.
On off, this is punched nicely but straight towards cover.
Bethell yorks Dhull here. Darted in very full and on middle and leg. Dhull just about manages to get his bat down in time.
Quicker one, skidding onto off. Dhull keeps it out.
FOUR! Hammered away! Short of a length, on off. Shaik Rasheed stays back and scythes it past backward point for a boundary. The boundary ruins what was turning out to be a good over. 5 runs from it.
Fuller in length, outside off. Shaik Rasheed went for the drive but it goes off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Short of a length, on off. Shaik Rasheed hops and steers it to backward point.
Good-length ball, on middle. Rasheed punches it back to the bowler.
Fuller, on leg. Yash Dhull drives it to long on for a single.
Short ball, on middle. Yash Dhull sways away from the line.
Full and on middle. pushed towards cover.
WIDE! Full and angling down the leg side. Shaik Rasheed looks to paddle it away but misses. Wided.
Flatter ball, on off. Shaik Rasheed gets behind the line and defends it out.
An arm ball, on off. Shaik Rasheed works it towards cover.
Flatter, full and on leg. Shaik Rasheed digs it out.
Loopy ball, on middle and leg. Dhull flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
50 up for India Under-19! On the pads, Shaik Rasheed clips it to square leg for a single.
Jacob Bethell is into the attack now.
Full and on off, Dhull drives it back to the bowler. A superb over from Tom Aspinwall. A wicket that England desperately needed and only a single off it.
Good-length ball, on off. Yash Dhull defends it to the off side.
Bangs it short once more but its well outside off, Dhull lets that one go
The skipper, Yash Dhull joins the vice-captain at the crease now.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! England Under-19 have got the breakthrough they were looking for. Back of a length, on leg. Harnoor Singh decides to leave the ball. He turns while he leaves the ball but it takes some part of the glove and goes behind to the keeper. Alex Horton puts his left hand and takes a sensational catch as the ball was flying over him. A wicket against the run of play. Can England Under-19 build on this now?
Commentary.Howout: c Alex Horton b Tom Aspinwall

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on middle. Shaik Rasheed pushes it to wide of mid-wicket for a run.
On a good length, on off. Rasheed plays it towards covers.

DRINKS! Joshua Boyden gave England the perfect start by sending the dangerous Angkrish Raghuvanshi back to the pavilion for a duck in the very first over. Since then though, Rasheed and Singh have taken their time to get settled and have eaten up a lot of deliveries. However, with no further wickets falling, England can only curtail the run rate for the time being. They need wickets to win this game or else the Indians will manage to stroll their way to victory.

A googly again, on middle. Tucked away to mid-wicket for a single. Both these batters are keeping the scoreboard ticking with these singles. They know that the boundaries will come and they just have to not giveaway their wicket.
A googly, outside off. Shaik Rasheed reads that one and defends it out.
Short and on off, punched down to long on for a run.
Full and on off, much quicker this time. Harnoor Singh presses forward and blocks.
Tossed up, on off. Rasheed with a lovely cover drive to sweeper cover for a single. He is limping a bit here. He might have just hit his boot as he played the cover drive.
FOUR! Down the leg side and Shaik Rasheed shuffles across to get inside the line of the ball and paddles it into the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Slower ball, full and outside off. Harnoor Singh drives it back to the bowler.
Length ball, leg-lined. Harnoor Singh works it to mid off off the outside half of the bat.
Back of a length, on off. Punched off the back foot through covers for a single.
On a length, on off. Rasheed blocks it towards point.
On a length ball, on off. Rasheed blocks it out.
Starts with a good-length ball, outside off. Shaik Rasheed drives it to point. The fielder there does well to stop the ball.
Tom Aspinwall is introduced into the attack now.

Optimistic appeal but not given. Fullish ball, down the leg side. Harnoor Singh looks to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire remains unmoved. Maiden over from Rehan Ahmed.
Here comes the wrong 'un. This is around off and spinning away. Singh leaves it alone.
Short again, Singh punches it off the back foot but straight towards cover-point.
Good fielding again. A tad bit short, Singh works it off the back foot but the can't get it through the packed off side field.
Sliding into middle and leg, Singh works it towards mid-wicket.
Ahmed comes 'round the wicket and tosses it up, on off. Singh pushes it out towards mid on.
Short again, outside off. Singh rocks back and cuts it behind point this time for another single. The run-rate is under 3 at the moment but wickets are the key here.
Shorter in length, angled across off. Rasheed punches it down the ground for a single.
Nicely flighted, around off. Rasheed defends it off the front foot.
Slower one, on a length and around middle and leg. Rasheed dabs it down towards square leg.
On the pads. This is worked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Sliding into middle and leg. Singh flicks it onto the leg side.
Outside off, cut away to deep point for a run.
Uppish but safe! Shorter one, around off and Singh hops on the back foot to cut. Singh mistimes it uppishly but just wide of short cover.
Tossed up again, fuller and on off. Rasheed drives it down to long off for a single.
Dot balls are good for England at the moment. Tossed up, around off and Rasheed works it towards mid on.
Around off, pushed away onto the off side.
Flatter delivery, outside off. Rasheed hangs back and punches it towards mid on.
Excellent over, just the single off it. On off, Singh backs away, looking to cut but mistimes it.
A touch shorter, on off. Rasheed goes on the back foot to work it through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted this time, on off. Rasheed defends it off the front foot.
Shorter, around off. Rasheed rocks back and cuts but can't get it past the cover-point fielder.
Quicker and flatter, on off. Rasheed keeps it out on the off side.
Nicely drifting in from outside off. Rasheed puts out a big stride forward to defend.
Flatter again, on middle. Singh just about manages to block it out.
On a length, around off and spinning away from the left-hander. Singh watchfully keeps it out.
Very full again, around off. Rasheed squeezes it out past point and picks up a single.
Quicker and fuller, on off. Rasheed flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter delivery, around off. Rasheed punches it off the back foot towards mid off.
Quicker through the air, on middle. Rasheed defends it onto the leg side.
The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 2! As many as 4 fielders can be kept outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over. Also, Rehan Ahmed is introduced into the attack.
A single to end the over! Tossed up, on off. Rasheed drives it to long on and retains the strike.
Flighted delivery, outside off. Rasheed hangs back and cuts it to backward point. George Thomas does well there to dive and stop the ball.
Tosses it up, on off. Rasheed is solid in his defence.
Flatter ball, on middle. Shaik Rasheed defends it to mid-wicket.
Tosses it up, on off. Pushed back to the bowler.
Slightly short, outside off. Shaik Rasheed defends it out with soft hands.
Full and outside off, Harnoor Singh blocks it out.

FOUR! Second boundary of the over! Just past the mid on fielder! Touch fuller, outside off. Harnoor Singh lifts it towards mid on. James Sales moves to his right and dives to catch it but the ball goes past him for a boundary. Great effort from Seales though.
On a good length, around off. Singh punches it off the back foot towards covers.
Fuller in length, outside off. Singh drives it off the toe end of the bat towards mid off.
Good-length ball, on middle. Turned to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Lovely shot! On the pads, Harnoor Singh flicks it with great timing on that one and it goes towards fine leg for a boundary.
Full and on off, pushed back to the bowler. Prest starts off with a maiden.

NOT OUT! Tosses this one up nicely, outside off. Rasheed presses forward and looks to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge. The keeper removes the bails in a flash and the umpire takes it upstairs as England appeal for stumping. Replay shows that Shaik Rasheed had his feet inside the crease.
Is that a stumping? Alex Horton with some quick hands behind the stumps and the decision is sent upstairs. The replay shows that Rasheed has his back foot firmly rooted inside the crease. NOT OUT!
Slightly short, outside off. Shaik Rasheed hangs back and works it towards point.
Quicker one, outside off. Shaik Rasheed defends it to the off side.
Full and on off, blocked out.
Starts with a tossed up delivery, on middle. Shaik Rasheed presses forward and defends it out.
The skipper, Tom Aspinwall ha brought himself on as first change.
Touch fuller, on off. Harnoor Singh defends it out.
Back of a length, around off. Singh gets behind the line and blocks it out.

Is that a dropped catch? No, it's not! Length ball, outside off. Harnoor Singh reaches out for it and looks to drive. The ball goes off the outside edge towards backward point. The fielder there dives to his right but the ball lands just short of him.
Back of a length, on middle. Singh works it on the leg side.
Length ball, outside off. Harnoor Singh shoulders arms.
On a good length, outside off. Harnoor Singh lets it sail through.
WIDE! England need to be careful here. They can't afford too many extras. Boyden sprays this one down the leg side. Singh leaves it alone. Wided.

In the air, but safe! On a length, on middle and leg. Harnoor Singh looks to tuck but closes the face of the bat a little early. The ball goes off the leading edge but falls way over mid-wicket. The batters cross ends.

FOUR! Excellent timing on that one! James Sales is persistent with his short deliveries. Bowls a short-of-a-length ball again, on middle. This time Harnoor Singh swivels and pulls it towards deep square leg for a boundary.
Four dots in a row now! Short of a length, on middle. Harnoor Singh defends it with ease.
Back of a length, on off. Harnoor Singh works it to mid-wicket.
On a good length, outside off. Harnoor Singh stays back and blocks it out.
Fuller and outside off. Harnoor Singh leans and drives it but finds the cover fielder.
Around middle and leg. Rasheed defends it out.
On a good length, around off. Rasheed pushes it back towards the bowler off the back foot.
Fullish ball, pushed across the right-hander. Rasheed with a solid front foot defense.
FOUR! Rasheed looks to be timing it well now. Around middle and leg, Rasheed works it through mid-wicket and the ball just races into the fence.
Excellent fielding yet again! Full, on off. Rasheed punches it with great timing but the skipper, Tom Prest sprints to his right at short cover and makes a brilliant stop.
Fullish ball, drifting onto the pads. Singh knocks it 'round the corner and picks up a single.
A length ball, around off. Rasheed stays solid in defense.

FOUR! Classy shot from Rasheed! Back of a length, around off. Rasheed hops and just caresses it off the back foot. The ball races through the cover region and ends up in the fence. First boundary of the innings for India.

WIDE! James Sales with a third wide in a row and that's not what you want while defending a small total. Rasheed advances and that puts off Sales a bit as he spills the slower bumper down the leg side.
WIDE! This time down the leg side. A length ball, angling down the leg side.
WIDE! Sales pushes this one wider but the ball ends up beyond the tramline. Wide signalled.
A good length ball, outside off. Rasheed makes a leave.
Shorter in length, around leg. Singh works it off his hips behind square for a single.
Pitched up, on off. Singh punches it nicely but right back to the bowler. Sales plucks out the ball and shows a bit of aggression by having a direct hit at the batter's end.
A length ball, well outside off. Singh watches it all the way and leaves it alone.
A third dot in a row to end another tidy over. Just the single off it. Around the hips, this is tucked away straight to square leg.
Full, angled across off. Rasheed leans in and pushes it towards cover.
Pitched up, around off. Rasheed presses forward to defend the ball under his eyeline.
Back of a length, angled into middle and leg. Singh pushes it to wide of mid on for a single.
A good-length delivery, on off. Singh taps it back onto the deck.
Nicely bowled! A length ball, into the corridor of uncertainty. Singh lets it through to the keeper.
This is pitched up, outside off. Rasheed shoulders arms.
A length ball, wide of off stump. Rasheed leaves it alone.
Brilliant fielding! Short and wide, Rasheed slaps it but Luxton with a brilliant dive to his left at short cover saves a certain boundary.
Back of a length, angled into the hips. Shaik Rasheed tucks it away behind square on the leg side and he is off the mark with a couple.
WIDE! Wayward from Sales. This is spilled way down the leg side.
Harnoor Singh and India are underway! On the pads, Singh flicks it away to fine leg for a single.
A fullish delivery, close to the off stump. Harnoor Singh makes an assured leave.
James Sales will steam in from the opposite end..
Fabulous stuff! A wicket-maiden to start off from Joshua Boyden! A length ball, on off. Rasheed presses forward to defend.
Good-length again, on off. Rasheed hops on the back foot and dabs it down on the off side.
This is pitched up, on off. Rasheed pushes it back to the bowler.
Right on the money again! Around the top of off. Rasheed blocks it out.
Shaik Rasheed walks out to bat at No.3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Joshua Boyden with a dream start! A good-length delivery, around off and just angling away. The line is just perfect. Angkrish Raghuvanshi hangs back and looks to push it out on the off side but the ball is just too close to his body. Raghuvanshi ends up edging it straight into the palms of the keeper and Alex Horton isn't going to drop that one. Raghuvanshi goes for a duck and England are right in this contest!
Commentary.Howout: c Alex Horton b Joshua Boyden

Commentary.Commentary: Boyden starts off with a fullish ball, wide of off stump. Raghuvanshi makes an easy leave.
